operations.description:
Retrieve email verification token details by its unique identifier.

This operation fetches the complete information of an email verification token, including its verification status, purpose, expiration time, and usage information. The verification token is used during member account registration or email address change operations to confirm ownership of the email address.

The verification token contains metadata including the associated email address, verification purpose ('registration' or 'email_change'), and expiration timestamp. The response indicates whether the token has been used, is still valid, or has expired. Note that the actual token string is NOT returned for security reasons.

This operation is typically used after a registration or email change request to verify the token's validity before completing the account creation or email update process. The system validates the token's validity, expiration status, and usage state before returning the verification details.

Related operations include member registration (POST /members) which generates verification tokens, and email change operations which also require verification token confirmation.

operations.specification:
Query multi_user_todo_member_email_verifications table by id (UUID primary key).

Validate the verification token exists and is not soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL).

Check token expiration: compare expires_at with current timestamp.

Check token usage: if used_at IS NOT NULL, token has been consumed.

Return verification details including:
- id: verification token UUID
- multiUserTodoMemberId: associated member ID (if any)
- token: the verification token string
- email: email address to be verified
- purpose: 'registration' or 'email_change'
- expiresAt: token expiration timestamp
- usedAt: timestamp when token was used (null if unused)
- createdAt: creation timestamp
- isValid: computed field indicating if token is valid (not expired, not used, not deleted)

Error handling:
- 404: Token not found or soft-deleted
- Return verification status without exposing sensitive token data to unauthorized parties

responseBody.description: Email verification token details with validation status (token string excluded for security)

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of edit history records for todo items owned by the authenticated member.

This operation provides comprehensive search capabilities for reviewing the modification history of todos. Each history entry captures a snapshot of the todo's state at the time of edit, including title, description, start date, and due date values. History entries are sorted from most recent to oldest by default.

Members can filter history entries by specific todo, date ranges, and field changes. The response includes summary information optimized for list displays, with full details available through individual history entry retrieval.

Access is restricted to history entries associated with todos owned by the authenticated member. Cross-user access is denied to protect data privacy and ownership boundaries.

Join with todos table to verify ownership relationship. Apply search filters on todo_id, changed_at date range, and field change indicators. Order by changed_at descending (most recent first). Return cursor-based pagination with summary data excluding full history entry details. Validate that all referenced todos belong to the authenticated member before returning results.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific edit history record for a todo item by its unique identifier.

This operation returns the complete snapshot of a todo's state at the time it was edited, capturing the values of title, description, start_date, and due_date fields as they existed when the modification occurred. The history entry includes the changed_at timestamp indicating when the edit was made, and the multi_user_todo_member_id identifying which member performed the change.

Access to history records is strictly controlled through member authentication. Only the member who owns the associated todo item can view its edit history. Cross-user access is denied to protect privacy and data isolation between users. If the requested history record belongs to a todo owned by another member, the system returns a 403 Forbidden error without revealing any information about the history entry's existence.

History records are retrieved by their unique UUID identifier (id field). The response includes all snapshot fields from the multi_user_todo_todo_histories table, allowing clients to review the complete state of a todo at any point in its edit history. This is particularly useful for auditing changes, understanding the evolution of a todo item, or recovering information about previous states.

The operation respects soft delete semantics. History records with a non-null deleted_at timestamp are excluded from results unless explicitly querying the trash. Permanently deleted history records (where deleted_at is set) return a 404 Not Found error.

Related operations include retrieving the parent todo item via its own endpoint, or listing all history entries for a todo through the history index operation.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query the multi_user_todo_todo_histories table by history ID (UUID). Perform authentication to identify the requesting member. Verify ownership by checking if the history record's associated todo belongs to the authenticated member. If ownership verification fails, return 403 Forbidden. If history record not found or permanently deleted, return 404 Not Found. On success, return the complete history record with all snapshot fields (title, description, start_date, due_date), the member ID who made the edit, the changed_at timestamp, and record metadata (created_at, updated_at). Apply soft delete filtering to exclude permanently deleted history entries unless explicitly querying trash.

responseBody.description: Complete edit history record from the multi_user_todo_todo_histories table with all snapshot fields and metadata. Contains the id (UUID primary key), multi_user_todo_member_id (UUID of the member who made the edit), changed_at (timestamp when the edit occurred), and snapshot fields: title, description, start_date, and due_date (all nullable, containing the values at the time of edit if those fields were modified). Also includes created_at and updated_at record timestamps. Snapshot fields are null if the corresponding todo field was not changed in that particular edit.
